messages:
jordan-support: FYI escalating — ACME says after the v2.14.0 model rollout their assistant responses became noticeably more concise and sometimes skip requested clarifications. They provided repro steps and samples below. Can we triage?
acme-customer: Copying what our users see. Prompt: 
```
You are an assistant that helps write clear onboarding emails for new users. Include 3 bullet points and one friendly sign-off.
```
API call: `POST /v1/generate` model=redwood-2.14.0 max_tokens=150 temp=0.2 stream=false 
Response (v2.14.0):
"Thanks. Here are the bullets."
(no sign-off, bullets are shorter than expected)
acme-customer: For comparison, when we were on redwood-2.13.7 same prompt produced 3 detailed bullets + "Best, <name>" sign-off. This started right after you rolled 2.14.0 to hosted. It affects our help flow.
deploy-bot: Model redwood-2.14.0 finished staged rollout -> hosted at 1876499800. Canary window OK per infra checks.
sam-ml: Thanks Jordan. Noted. First guess: either system prompt/objective changed or a safety/length truncation tweak got applied. Do we have their request-id?
jordan-support: request-id from customer: req_0a9f3b2c. Also they attached raw response body and token usage: prompt_tokens=42 completion_tokens=18 total_tokens=60.
indra: 18 completion tokens is tiny. Either the model is sampling very conservative or `max_tokens`/stop sequences are being respected differently. Ask them to repro with `max_tokens=400` and `stream=true` (to rule out truncation at the API layer).
acme-customer: Will try & report back. Quick note: we didn't change our client. We only noticed after your rollout.
jordan-support: Action: collect a failing request trace + full raw output. Elaine can you pull the server-side logs for req_0a9f3b2c and the rollout diffs?
elaine-ops: On it. Pulling traces now. Preliminary look: the rollout included a tweak to default `response_length_weight` in the runtime config (internal flag) — flagged in the deploy notes as "reduce verbosity for short prompts". I'm pulling the exact diff.
sam-ml: That flag would match symptoms. We should run the customer's prompt through the old and new model binaries locally with identical decode settings. I'll run evals comparing v2.13.7 vs v2.14.0 with their prompt set.
indra: Also check if any tokenization/stop-sequence behavior changed — sometimes newline-handling or system prompt trimming can cut completions short.
acme-customer: Ran with `max_tokens=400` and `stream=true` — still short output. Attached trace id: client_req_1876504001.
elaine-ops: Got client_req_1876504001. Server logs show early termination at decode step due to the `response_length_weight` heuristic hitting a threshold for this prompt.
sam-ml: OK that confirms model-side preference change. Quick mitigations: 1) route ACME traffic to v2.13.7 routing tag 2) patch runtime to expose `response_length_weight` override per-request 3) run a targeted eval across top enterprise customers for regressions. Which should we do first?
jordan-support: ACME asked for fast fix — they asked to be routed back if possible. I think routing them ASAP is highest priority.
indra: Agreed. Elaine can implement customer-scoped routing to stable model version for now. Also need a postmortem on why this flag was toggled without broader eval on business-critical prompts.
elaine-ops: I can add routing rule for acme-customer -> redwood-2.13.7 by EOD. Also starting a debug build that disables the heuristic in runtime to test behavior.
sam-ml: I'll start the eval harness and throw their prompt set plus a small representative corpus. If we see consistent brevity skew, we'll revert the flag in the next patch.
jordan-support: Owners: elaine-ops (routing & logs) sam-ml (eval + repro), indra (customer comms + rollout review). Jordan will coordinate with ACME and update them.
acme-customer: Appreciate the fast response. If you can route us back now it's perfect. We depend on the elaborative bullets.
indra: @acme-customer routing change in progress. Expecting switch within 30 mins. We'll follow up once traffic is on v2.13.7 and confirm outputs.
elaine-ops: Routing applied for acme-customer -> redwood-2.13.7. Verified a few sample requests now return the fuller bullets + sign-off.
jordan-support: Great. Please keep thread updated and file a regression ticket (ENG-6643) for the runtime change and add ACME repro prompts to the test corpus.
sam-ml: Filed ENG-6643. I'll attach evaluation artifacts and diff results once done. Early signal: v2.14.0 has a systematic brevity bias on prompts that include instruction-like metadata.
indra: We'll also update rollout checklist: require automated evaluation on a set of enterprise prompts and a guardrail for `response_length_weight` changes.
jordan-support: Thanks team. ACME — we'll follow up with timeline for permanent fix. :thumbsup:
